newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Information seen key to African oil investment.
newsitem.headline: Information seen key to African oil investment.

text.p: Information was critical to drawing overseas players to invest in African oil and gas exploration, Colin Wilkinson, vice president of Argentine company Pluspetrol International Inc, said on Wednesday.

Reiterating what many other delegates to the Africa Upstream 1996 conference had said, Wilkinson urged African states to offer attractive incentives to overseas oil and gas exploration and development companies.
"Companies are bringing major investment funds and do need incentives. The availability of information is very, very critical and information is not always readily accessible," Wilkinson said.
Pluspetrol focused on high-value reserves worldwide and concentrated its activity in known oil and gas producing areas.
"We are not in the business of drilling for oil. We are in the business of drilling for dollars," he said.
He said companies required stable and attractive fiscal regimes to invest in countries, but that very often those states with the proven reserves were lacking in such regimes.
While these countries could still draw investment, Pluspetrol found it hard to invest in countries where the national oil companies were dominant and where sanctions were imposed, Wilkinson said.
Nevertheless, Pluspetrol was involved in north and west Africa, particularly in Algeria, Tunisia and Egypt.
